name: MI-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Lisa McClain with $5.2M raised and no outside opposition
Democratic challenger Ray Pooley raised only ~$8K
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: McClain is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by sixteen points, while Pooley has raised almost nothing and drawn no outside spending. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A major late Democratic outside-spending push or a polling surprise could narrow the margin, though nothing currently signals competitive interest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lisa McClain seeks reelection in a Michigan district that voted Republican by about sixteen points at the presidential level. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised over five million dollars and holding more than a million and a half on hand, with no outside groups opposing her. Challenger Ray Pooley has raised under ten thousand dollars, and minor-party and independent candidates round out a sparse ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give McClain roughly a ninety-five percent chance of winning. The fundamentals, money gap, and district lean all align, making this a safe Republican seat with little evidence of a competitive contest developing.
